summary: Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MA in religious studies at Naropa University. He studied under Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Tsultrim Allione, and others.

Ryan Richard Overbey is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an AB from Brown (1997–2001) and a PhD from Harvard (2001–2010), later holding posts at UC Berkeley (2013–2015), Wesleyan (attested 2016), and Skidmore College (2017).
Ryo Kuroiwa works in computational fields and Indology. Kuroiwa has held posts at the National Institute of Informatics and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Ryo Nishimura (1972–2016) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University from circa 1991 to 2002 under Fumihiko Sueki.
Ryōshō Taira (1906–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as professor emeritus at Taisho University, where his posts are attested in 1976 and 1984.
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015–2026) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara (1909–2000) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Humboldt University of Berlin under Shun'ichi Takagi, Ryujo Yamada, and Ryotai Hatani. He later lectured at Humboldt and was a professor at Ryukoku (attested 1963–1974).
Ryoichi Kondo (1930–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryoji Kishino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. In 2026, Kishino was attested as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryojin Soga (1875–1971) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shinshu and Otani Universities under Manshi Kiyozawa. He was a professor at Toyo University (1916–1924) and held professorships and the presidency (1961–1967) at Otani University.

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Mitomo served as a professor at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Ryokei Kaginushi (1926–2005) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as a professor in the Faculty of Letters at Otani University, attested in 1978 and 1993.
Ryoken Nawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. Nawa served as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2020–2026).
Ryoko Mochizuki (born 1933) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo until 1963 and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1972 and 1983).

Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872–1946) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz and Alfred Foucher, and later held professorships at the Third Higher School (1899) and Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Toyo University. He served as a professor (from 1973) and professor emeritus (2007) at Taisho University, and as a visiting professor at Shuchiin University (2012).

Ryoshin Nakao (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1971–1980). Nakao has served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1990) and as a staff member at the Research Institute of Soto Studies.

Ryosho Hayashi (1927–2008) was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Taisho and Tokyo Metropolitan Universities. He served as a professor (1975), Dean of Letters (1981), and professor emeritus (1990–1994) at Taisho University.

Ryosho Nakamura (born 1927) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Tohoku University (~1949–1953) under Ensho Kanakura, earned a doctorate from Rissho University (1977), and served as a professor at Kagoshima International University (attested 1991).
